title: VSEPR Theory and Shapes of Simple Molecules
notes: **VSEPR principle:** electron pairs around a central atom arrange themselves to minimize repulsion. Both bonding pairs and lone pairs repel, but lone pairs repel more strongly.
**Linear (2 electron domains):** $BeF_2$, $CO_2$. Bond angle 180Â°. No lone pairs on central atom.
**Trigonal planar (3 domains):** $BF_3$. Bond angle 120Â°. No lone pairs.
**Tetrahedral (4 domains):** $CH_4$. Bond angle 109.5Â°. No lone pairs. $CH_3Cl$ is also tetrahedral but bond angles are slightly distorted because Cl is more electronegative than H.
**Trigonal bipyramidal (5 domains):** $PCl_5$. Axial bonds are longer and at 90Â° to equatorial bonds.

**Bent (2 bonds + 1 or 2 lone pairs):** $H_2O$ has 2 lone pairs, bond angle 104.5Â° (compressed from 109.5Â°). $H_2S$ is bent but with smaller angle (~92Â°) because S is larger and less electronegative than O.
**Trigonal pyramidal (3 bonds + 1 lone pair):** $NH_3$. Bond angle 107Â° (compressed from 109.5Â°). $PH_3$ is also pyramidal but with smaller angle (~93Â°) because P is larger.
